title: The English Words Only Koreans Understand

slides.headline: Koreans use English words **no English speaker knows.**
It's called **Konglish**
slides.body: Konglish (콩글리시) means English-looking words made in Korea. Koreans use them daily. Native speakers often have no idea.

slides.headline: Borrowed, then **remade**
slides.body: Many English words came in through Japanese or after the Korean War. Then Koreans reshaped them to fit their own use.

slides.headline: Hand phone. **Eye shopping.**
slides.body: A cell phone is a "hand phone" (핸드폰). Window shopping is "eye shopping". Both make sense once you hear them.

slides.headline: Fighting! means **you've got this**
slides.body: "Fighting" (파이팅) is a cheer, not a threat. Koreans say it before exams, interviews and games.

slides.headline: Short, catchy, **and everyone gets it**
slides.body: To Koreans these aren't English mistakes. They're everyday Korean words that just happen to look English.

slides.headline: Your language **does it too**
slides.body: Germans call a cell phone a "Handy". Every language borrows English and bends it. Korea just does it loudly.

slides.headline: The price of **"service"**
slides.body: In a Korean restaurant, "service" (서비스) means a free extra dish from the owner. No charge.

slides.headline: Not bad English. **Korean.**
slides.body: Konglish was never made for English speakers. It's Korean, built from English parts.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
In Korea, a cell phone is a "hand phone" and "Fighting!" means you've got this: welcome to Konglish, the English words only Koreans understand.

They're not mistakes. They're Korean words built from English parts, and Koreans use them every day.

Which English word does your language use in its own way?
reply: One more: "skinship" (a Konglish word) means casual affectionate touch, like holding hands or a hug between friends or couples. Koreans talk about it all the time, and visitors usually guess it's about skincare. Which English word does your language use in a way English speakers would never recognize?
fact_check: 3장: 외래어 일부가 일본어 경유(핸들 등)·전후 미군 영향으로 들어온 것은 일반적 설명.
5장: 파이팅은 응원 표현. 국립국어원 순화어 '아자'가 있으나 생략.
8장: 식당 '서비스'=무료 추가 음식. 통계 아닌 '0원' 표현.
댓글: 스킨십=신체 접촉 애정 표현, 콩글리시(일본 경유설 있음, 생략).
